article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar', report warns

tasks.prompt: What is the report's central warning?
options: Official figures may miss many teenagers enrolled in college but rarely attending
Most English colleges no longer teach maths or English
Young people are leaving college only because they have full-time jobs
School attendance in England is higher than ever
tasks.correct_answer: Official figures may miss many teenagers enrolled in college but rarely attending
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הדו״ח מזהיר שעשרות אלפי בני 16–17 רשומים כלומדים אך נעדרים הרבה, ולכן אינם מופיעים כראוי בנתונים הרשמיים על NEET.

tasks.prompt: What does the report mean by “severely absent”?
options: Missing at least 10% of college sessions
Missing at least half of college sessions
Failing one GCSE examination
Changing college during the year
tasks.correct_answer: Missing at least half of college sessions
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בדו״ח severely absent מוגדר כהיעדרות מלפחות מחצית ממפגשי הלימוד במכללה.

tasks.prompt: What does “under the radar” mean in the article?
options: Studying through an online tracking system
Travelling to college by bus
Going unnoticed by official monitoring and support
Being formally removed from a college roll
tasks.correct_answer: Going unnoticed by official monitoring and support
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מתאר בני נוער שאינם מזוהים בנתונים הרשמיים ולכן גם אינם מקבלים את התמיכה הדרושה.

tasks.prompt: Which change has Bolton College introduced to improve attendance?
options: It has ended all part-time courses
It gives every student a £30 payment each morning
It allows students to skip compulsory GCSE classes
It employs full-time positive engagement officers to greet and contact students
tasks.correct_answer: It employs full-time positive engagement officers to greet and contact students
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המכללה הציבה אנשי קשר במשרה מלאה שמקבלים את פני התלמידים בבוקר ויוצרים קשר עם מי שלא הגיע.

tasks.prompt: Why can a £30 work shift sometimes matter more to a student than a future qualification?
options: The qualification is guaranteed to have no value
Immediate financial pressure can outweigh a benefit expected months later
Colleges require students to work during every lesson
Part-time work automatically counts as a GCSE pass
tasks.correct_answer: Immediate financial pressure can outweigh a benefit expected months later
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לסטודנט הזקוק להכנסה כעת, תשלום מיידי ממשמרת עשוי להיות חשוב יותר מתועלת של הסמכה שתגיע רק בעוד חודשים.

tasks.prompt: What does “tailored support” mean in the Association of Colleges' response?
options: Punishment that is identical for every absent student
Support designed for the particular needs of individual students
A national list of college examination dates
Free uniforms made by local employers
tasks.correct_answer: Support designed for the particular needs of individual students
tasks.explanation_hebrew: tailored support היא תמיכה מותאמת לצרכים האישיים של התלמיד, כגון קשיי בריאות הנפש, תחבורה או עבודה.

tasks.prompt: Distinguish the two meanings of “hidden Neets” used in the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשוות במדויק בין הגדרת דוח נציבת הילדים לבין ההגדרה בדוח הביניים של אלן מילברן.
expected_points: Dame Rachel's report uses the term for students enrolled in college but persistently absent
These students may appear in official records as being in education
The report argues they should be counted alongside official Neets
Milburn's interim report uses the term for people who are Neet
Those people are also not claiming benefits
Not claiming benefits makes them harder for services to find and reach

tasks.prompt: Explain why simply enrolling a teenager in college does not prove that the teenager is receiving education or support.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את הפער בין רישום לנוכחות, את היעדר חובת הדיווח ואת ההשלכות על זיהוי צעירים פגיעים.
expected_points: A student can remain enrolled while missing many sessions
Around 42,000 enrolled 16- and 17-year-olds missed at least half their sessions
Colleges are not currently required to collect or report attendance data like schools
The DfE therefore lacks a complete central picture
Official status may hide practical disengagement from education
Vulnerable students can go unnoticed
Without identification they may not receive mental-health, travel or other tailored support

tasks.prompt: Summarise the scale, causes and proposed responses to persistent college absence among 16- and 17-year-olds.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את הנתונים המרכזיים, גורמי ההיעדרות, אוכלוסיות בסיכון והמלצות הדו״ח והממשלה.
expected_points: The report used data from 262 college groups in England
An estimated 52.2% were persistently absent under the school definition
Around 42,000, or 5.9%, were severely absent
The official estimate lists 57,000 16- and 17-year-olds as Neet
Causes include part-time work, travel costs and post-pandemic disengagement
Severely absent students may have mental-health challenges or other vulnerabilities
Recommendations include national attendance data and targets
The report calls for faster mental-health support, better work experience and free bus travel
The DfE plans central attendance tracking and a stepping-stone qualification

tasks.prompt: Write a short policy proposal for reducing severe absence at further-education colleges.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית הצעה המבוססת על חסמים ופתרונות שבכתבה, עם מדידה, תמיכה מותאמת ויישום מעשי.
expected_points: Require consistent collection of attendance data
Set clear targets while avoiding punishment-only responses
Contact students quickly after missed sessions
Expand mental-health support teams
Address travel costs, for example through free bus travel
Recognise conflicts with part-time employment
Provide tailored support for vulnerable students
Improve work experience and employer engagement
Consider alternatives to repeated GCSE failure and resits
Explain how progress would be measured
